examples.ko: 아이마다 한글을 배우기 좋은 적령기가 다르니 서두를 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: Every child has a different best age to learn Hangul, so there's no need to rush.

examples.ko: 취학 적령기를 앞둔 아이의 부모들은 입학 준비로 바빠요.
examples.en: Parents of children nearing school age are busy preparing for enrollment.

examples.ko: 결혼 적령기라는 말이 요즘은 점점 사라지고 있어요.
examples.en: The idea of a 'right age to marry' is fading these days.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 아직 학교에 갈 적령이 아니에요.
examples.en: My child isn't old enough to go to school yet.

examples.ko: 적령기에 시작하면 훨씬 빨리 배운다고 해요.
examples.en: They say you learn much faster if you start at the right age.

examples.ko: 이 책은 취학 적령기 아이들이 읽기에 딱 좋아요.
examples.en: This book is just right for children of school-starting age.

explain: '적령'보다 뒤에 '기'를 붙인 '적령기'로 훨씬 자주 말해요. '취학 적령기', '결혼 적령기'처럼 앞에 어떤 일인지를 붙여서 그 일을 하기에 알맞은 나이를 나타내요. 일상에서는 '알맞은 나이'라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used far more often as '적령기' than as '적령' alone. You put the activity before it, as in '취학 적령기' or '결혼 적령기', to mean the suitable age for that activity. In everyday talk people also say '알맞은 나이' (the fitting age).

examples.ko: 이사 간 첫날 밤에 집 안의 적막감이 낯설었어요.
examples.en: On the first night after moving, the stillness of the house felt strange.
After the exam ended, even a hush settled over the classroom.

examples.ko: 아이들이 모두 떠나자 집에는 적막감만 남았어요.
examples.en: After the children all left, only emptiness and silence remained in the house.

examples.ko: 눈 내린 새벽 거리에서 묘한 적막감을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: I felt a strange stillness on the street at snowy dawn.

examples.ko: 갑자기 전기가 나가서 갑작스러운 적막감에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The power suddenly went out, and the abrupt silence startled me.

examples.ko: 큰 행사가 끝난 뒤의 적막감도 은근히 힘들어요.
examples.en: The lonely quiet after a big event is quietly hard too.

explain: '고요함'은 소리가 없는 상태이고, '적막감'은 조용해서 쓸쓸하고 허전한 느낌까지 담겨 있어요. '적막감이 감돌다', '적막감이 흐르다'처럼 자주 말해요. 사람이 떠난 뒤나 큰일이 끝난 뒤의 분위기에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '고요함' just means no sound, while '적막감' also carries a lonely, empty feeling. It is often used as '적막감이 감돌다' or '적막감이 흐르다'. It fits the mood after people leave or after a big event ends.

examples.en: Today's snowfall in Seoul is 5 centimeters.
The snow depth increased overnight, so I'm worried about the commute.

examples.ko: 산간 지역의 적설량도 꽤 많을 거래요.
examples.en: They say the snowfall in the mountain areas will be quite heavy too.
The news reported the snowfall by region.

examples.ko: 적설량에 따라 제설 작업 계획이 달라져요.
examples.en: The snow-clearing plan changes depending on the snowfall.

examples.ko: 눈이 그쳤는데도 적설량 때문에 길이 아직 위험해요.
examples.en: Even though the snow stopped, the roads are still dangerous because of the accumulated snow.

explain: 일기예보에서 '비가 얼마나 왔는지'는 '강수량', '눈이 얼마나 쌓였는지'는 '적설량'이라고 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '눈이 10센티 왔어요'처럼 말하고, '적설량'은 뉴스와 예보에서 많이 들려요.
explain_en: In weather reports, '강수량' is how much rain fell and '적설량' is how much snow has piled up. In daily talk people say '눈이 10센티 왔어요', and '적설량' is mostly heard in news and forecasts.

examples.ko: 달리기에서는 아무도 그의 적수가 못 돼요.
examples.en: In running, nobody is a match for him.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 결승전에서 만만치 않은 적수를 만났어요.
examples.en: That player met a formidable opponent in the final.
My younger sibling is no match for me in games.
The two are famous as long-time rivals.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 바둑에서 서로 좋은 적수였어요.
examples.en: Since childhood, we have been good rivals in Go.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 적수 없이 일곱 번 연속 우승했어요.
examples.en: That team won seven championships in a row without a rival.

explain: '적'은 싸우는 상대지만 '적수'는 실력을 겨루는 상대예요. '적수가 없다', '적수가 못 되다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 쓰는 일이 많아요. '라이벌'과 비슷하지만 '적수'는 실력이 맞먹는다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: '적' is an enemy you fight, but '적수' is someone you compete with on skill. It is often used with negatives, as in '적수가 없다' or '적수가 못 되다'. It is close to 'rival', but '적수' stresses that the two are evenly matched in ability.

examples.ko: 회사 세계는 적자생존이라고 말하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say the business world is survival of the fittest.
In the market, the law of survival of the fittest applies as it is.
The job market these days is truly survival of the fittest.
If you can't adapt to change, you get pushed out of the survival race.
It's not only the animal world that is survival of the fittest.
I'm worried about the survival-of-the-fittest style of competitive culture.

explain: 원래는 진화론에서 나온 말인데, 일상에서는 경쟁이 치열한 사회나 회사를 비유할 때 많이 써요. '약육강식'은 힘센 쪽이 약한 쪽을 누른다는 느낌이고, '적자생존'은 환경에 잘 맞는 쪽이 살아남는다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It comes from evolutionary theory, but in daily life people often use it to describe fiercely competitive societies or workplaces. '약육강식' feels like the strong overpower the weak, while '적자생존' feels like those who fit the environment survive.

examples.en: I was quite surprised to hear the news.
This incident was emotionally quite hard on me.
It cost a good deal more than I expected.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 사람들 앞에서 적잖이 긴장했어요.
examples.en: I got pretty nervous in front of people I'd just met.

examples.ko: 아이가 갑자기 울어서 부모님이 적잖이 당황하셨어요.
examples.en: The child suddenly cried, and the parents were quite flustered.

examples.ko: 그 일은 우리 팀에 적잖이 도움이 됐어요.
examples.en: That work helped our team quite a lot.

explain: '적지 않게'라는 뜻이지만 '많이'보다 말하는 사람이 정도를 눈여겨본다는 느낌이 있어요. '놀라다', '당황하다', '실망하다' 같은 감정을 나타내는 말과 특히 자주 써요. 말할 때는 '꽤'나 '많이'를 더 자주 쓰고, '적잖이'는 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It means 'not a little', and it sounds like the speaker is noting how big the degree is. It is especially common with emotion verbs such as 놀라다, 당황하다 and 실망하다. In speech people use '꽤' or '많이' more often, while '적잖이' shows up more in writing and slightly formal speech.

examples.en: This truck's load capacity is 5 tons.
If you go over the load limit, you have to pay a fine.
I have a lot of moving stuff, so I'm worried about the load capacity.
We split the cargo to fit the load capacity.

examples.ko: 이 작은 승합차는 적재량도 꽤 커요.
examples.en: This small van has a fairly large load capacity too.
It's safer to load less than the maximum capacity.

explain: 트럭이나 배 같은 운송 수단이 실을 수 있는 양을 말해요. '최대 적재량', '적재량 초과'처럼 규정과 안전 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 짐을 싣는 칸은 '적재함'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to how much a vehicle such as a truck or ship can carry. It often appears in talk of rules and safety, as in '최대 적재량' or '적재량 초과'. The cargo space itself is called '적재함'.

en: the right person or thing in the right place

examples.en: It's important to place people in the right positions.
Putting the right people in the right places is a company's strength.

examples.ko: 적재적소 배치 덕분에 팀이 잘 돌아가요.
examples.en: Thanks to the right placement, the team runs well.

examples.ko: 물건이 적재적소에 놓여 있으니 찾기 쉬워요.
examples.en: Things are in the right places, so they're easy to find.
Money is worth something only when spent in the right place.

examples.ko: 적재적소에 쓸 말을 고르는 게 어려워요.
examples.en: Choosing the right word to use at the right moment is hard.

explain: 주로 '적재적소에 배치하다/쓰다/두다'처럼 써요. 사람을 자리에 맞게 앉힐 때 가장 많이 쓰지만 물건, 돈, 말에도 써요. 회사나 면접 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is mainly used as '적재적소에 배치하다/쓰다/두다'. It is most common when placing people in suitable posts, but it also works for things, money and words. You often hear it in talk about companies and job interviews.

examples.en: We loaded the moving boxes into the truck's cargo bed.

examples.ko: 적재함 문이 열려 있어서 짐이 떨어질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The cargo door was open, so the load almost fell out.

examples.ko: 짐을 다 내려서 적재함이 텅 비었어요.
examples.en: We unloaded everything, so the cargo area is totally empty.
Please cover the cargo bed with a cover.
The man is taking boxes down from the cargo bed.
I rented a truck with a wide cargo bed.

explain: 트럭 뒤쪽의 짐 싣는 칸이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '짐칸'이라고 많이 말하고, '적재함'은 설명이나 안내문에서 더 자주 보여요. 실을 수 있는 양은 '적재량'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the part at the back of a truck where cargo goes. In daily talk people often say '짐칸', while '적재함' appears more in explanations and notices. The amount it can hold is called '적재량'.

examples.en: My home, where I live alone, feels lonely sometimes.

examples.ko: 아이들이 독립한 뒤로 집이 적적하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Since the kids moved out, the house feels lonely.
I call Grandma often in case she feels lonely.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 혼자 있으니 적적한 기분이 들어요.
examples.en: Being alone on a rainy day makes me feel lonely.
When it feels lonely, I leave the radio on.
My friend moved away, so the neighborhood feels lonely now.

explain: '외롭다'는 마음이 쓸쓸한 것이고, '적적하다'는 주변이 조용하고 사람이 없어서 허전한 것에 더 가까워요. 혼자 지내는 어르신 이야기에서 특히 자주 들려요. 어른께는 '적적하시겠어요'처럼 '-시-'를 넣어 말해요.
explain_en: '외롭다' is about a lonely heart, while '적적하다' is closer to feeling empty because the surroundings are quiet and nobody is around. You hear it often when talking about elderly people living alone. For an elder, add '-시-', as in '적적하시겠어요'.

examples.ko: 이 중고 자전거 가격이 적정가인지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I don't know if this used bike's price is fair.

examples.ko: 사기 전에 여러 가게의 적정가를 비교해 보세요.
examples.en: Before buying, compare the fair prices at several stores.
I think this is a fair price.
That house was listed higher than the fair price.

examples.ko: 적정가에 팔려고 가격을 여러 번 조정했어요.
examples.en: I adjusted the price several times to sell at a fair price.
The fair price changes depending on market conditions.

explain: 일상에서는 '적당한 가격'이라고 많이 말하고, '적정가'는 중고 거래나 부동산, 시장 이야기에서 자주 써요. '시세'는 지금 실제로 거래되는 값이고, '적정가'는 알맞다고 보는 값이에요.
explain_en: In daily talk people often say '적당한 가격', and '적정가' is used more in second-hand deals, real estate and market talk. '시세' is the price currently being traded at, while '적정가' is the price seen as fair.

examples.en: About 30 percent of your salary is a reasonable level for rent.
We need to keep the cost at a reasonable level.
If the number of people goes above a reasonable level, meetings get longer.
It's good to keep gifts within a reasonable limit.
Try making a plan within a reasonable range.
The proper limit of a conversation differs from person to person.

explain: '선'이 붙어서 넘으면 안 되는 경계라는 느낌이 있어서 '적정선을 넘다/지키다/맞추다'처럼 자주 써요. 금액이나 인원 같은 숫자뿐 아니라 행동의 정도에도 쓸 수 있어요. 값 자체를 말하는 '적정가'와는 달라요.
explain_en: Because of '선' (line), it feels like a boundary you shouldn't cross, so it is often used as '적정선을 넘다/지키다/맞추다'. It works for numbers like money or headcount and also for the degree of behavior. It differs from '적정가', which is about the price itself.

examples.ko: 택배가 한꺼번에 몰려서 물류센터에 물량이 적체돼요.
examples.en: Parcels came all at once, so goods are piling up at the logistics center.

examples.ko: 연휴 뒤에 업무가 적체되어 야근이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Work backed up after the holidays, so overtime increased.
Handle the documents every day so they don't pile up.

examples.ko: 퇴근 시간에는 차들이 적체돼서 움직이지 않아요.
examples.en: At rush hour, the cars are jammed and not moving.

examples.ko: 민원이 적체된 탓에 답변이 늦어지고 있어요.
examples.en: Replies are slow because complaints have piled up.
If stock piles up, warehouse costs grow.

explain: '쌓이다'가 그냥 많아지는 것이라면 '적체되다'는 쌓여서 흐르지 못하고 막혀 있다는 느낌이 있어요. 일상에서는 '밀리다'를 많이 쓰고, '적체'는 업무나 물류, 교통 이야기와 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. '교통 적체', '업무 적체'처럼 명사로도 써요.
explain_en: '쌓이다' just means things accumulate, while '적체되다' adds the sense of being stuck and unable to flow. In daily talk people often say '밀리다', and '적체' is heard more in business, logistics, traffic and news. It also works as a noun, as in '교통 적체' or '업무 적체'.

examples.ko: 회사가 어제 전격적 인사 발표를 했어요.
examples.en: The company made a sudden personnel announcement yesterday.
The two countries suddenly reached an agreement.
The boss abruptly changed the plan.
It was such a sudden decision that everyone was surprised.
That singer abruptly announced retirement.

examples.ko: 전격적인 발표 때문에 주가가 크게 움직였어요.
examples.en: The stock price moved a lot because of the sudden announcement.

explain: '갑자기'보다 뉴스 느낌이 강하고, 결정·발표·합의·발탁처럼 중요한 일에 주로 써요. 사람의 평범한 행동에는 어울리지 않아서 '갑자기 일어났어요'처럼 말하는 게 자연스러워요. 보통 '전격적으로', '전격적인' 형태로 나와요.
explain_en: It sounds more like news than '갑자기' and is mostly used for important matters such as decisions, announcements, agreements and appointments. It doesn't fit ordinary behavior, where '갑자기' is more natural. It usually appears as '전격적으로' or '전격적인'.

examples.en: My younger sibling became a resident in internal medicine this time.
The residents look after patients all night.
I heard the hospital is recruiting new residents.

examples.ko: 전공의는 보통 일이 많아서 잠을 거의 못 자요.
examples.en: Residents usually have so much work that they barely sleep.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 전공의 근무 시간 이야기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news talked about residents' working hours.
My father worked as a resident when he was young.

explain: 전문의가 되기 위해 병원에서 일하며 수련을 받는 의사를 말해요. 영어의 '레지던트'에 해당하고, 의대를 졸업하고 면허를 딴 뒤 들어가는 과정이에요. 의료 뉴스에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a doctor who works and trains at a hospital to become a specialist. It corresponds to the English 'resident', and the training begins after a doctor graduates from medical school and gets a license. It appears often in medical news.

examples.en: He snatched the ball as fast as lightning.
I finished the work at lightning speed.
The thief vanished in a flash.

examples.ko: 상대 팀의 전광석화와 같은 공격에 당했어요.
examples.en: We were hit by the other team's lightning-fast attack.

examples.ko: 전광석화 같은 판단 덕분에 사고를 피했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to a lightning-quick decision, we avoided an accident.
The cat jumped up like a flash of lightning.

explain: 아주 빠른 움직임이나 판단을 말할 때 쓰고, '전광석화처럼', '전광석화 같은'의 형태로 자주 나와요. 평소 대화에서는 '번개같이'라고 더 많이 말하고, 스포츠 중계나 글에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It describes very fast movement or judgment and often appears as '전광석화처럼' or '전광석화 같은'. In everyday talk people say '번개같이' more often, while this word shows up in sports commentary and writing.

examples.en: Outdated practices now need to be fixed.
The company's outdated culture is the problem.
There are still places that work in an outdated way.
Young people leave because of an outdated mindset.
The rules are so outdated that they're inconvenient.
Many people say we should change the outdated system.

explain: 제도, 관행, 사고방식이 시대에 뒤떨어졌다고 비판할 때 써요. '구식'보다 훨씬 무겁고 비판하는 느낌이 강해서 사람에게 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 뉴스와 글에서 '전근대적 관행'이라는 말을 자주 봐요.
explain_en: It criticizes systems, customs or ways of thinking as behind the times. It is much heavier and more critical than '구식', so using it about a person can be rude. In news and writing you often see '전근대적 관행'.

examples.en: That player is a promising rookie.
A promising young man received a big award.
This field will stay promising in the future.
He was promising, but he took a break because of his health.
I applied to a company that looks promising.
My parents always say I have a bright future.

explain: 앞날에 좋은 가능성이 크다는 뜻으로, 신인, 청년, 분야처럼 앞으로 크게 될 것에 써요. 말할 때는 '유망하다'만 써도 충분해요. 같은 뜻의 '전도양양하다'는 훨씬 드물어요.
explain_en: It says someone or something has great potential ahead, and is used for rookies, young people and fields expected to grow. In speech, just '유망하다' is enough. The similar '전도양양하다' is much rarer.

examples.en: He is known as an outstanding strategist.
Our team's coach is a great strategist.

examples.ko: 좋은 전략가가 있어야 팀이 이길 수 있어요.
examples.en: A team needs a good strategist in order to win.

examples.ko: 게임에서는 제가 늘 전략가 역할을 맡아요.
examples.en: In games, I always take the role of strategist.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 전략가들이 새 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: The company's strategists drew up a new plan.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 체스를 두면 전략가처럼 생각해요.
examples.en: My friend thinks like a strategist when playing chess.

explain: 군사뿐 아니라 회사 경영, 스포츠, 게임처럼 계획을 세워 이기는 일에 두루 써요. 곁에서 의견을 내며 돕는 사람은 '참모'라고 해서 '전략가'와 조금 달라요. '정치 전략가', '마케팅 전략가'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여도 돼요.
explain_en: It is used not only in the military but also in business, sports and games for someone who plans in order to win. An adviser who helps from the side is called a '참모', which differs a bit from '전략가'. You can add a field before it, as in '정치 전략가' or '마케팅 전략가'.

examples.en: That player gave it his all down to the last pitch.
I decided to give it everything for this exam.
I'm putting all my effort into exam prep right now.
I threw myself into the project and got good results.
If you don't give it your all, you'll regret it later.
Whatever it is, if you put everything into it, a way opens up.

explain: 원래는 야구에서 힘을 다해 공을 던진다는 말인데, 지금은 어떤 일에 온 힘을 쏟을 때 두루 써요. 일상에서는 '최선을 다하다'나 '올인하다'가 더 가볍고 자연스러워요. '~에 전력투구하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: It started in baseball as throwing with all your strength, but now it is used broadly for pouring everything into a task. In daily talk, '최선을 다하다' or '올인하다' feels lighter and more natural. It is used with the particle '에', as in '~에 전력투구하다'.

examples.en: This year's box office success of the film was unprecedented.
That athlete set an unprecedented record.
Nothing like this had ever happened, so everyone was surprised.
He is called a genius like no other.
It was such a big event that you could call it one of a kind.
It's a drama that enjoyed unparalleled popularity.

explain: 이전에도 없었고 앞으로도 없을 것 같다는 뜻이라 기록이나 업적을 크게 칭찬할 때 써요. '유례없다'는 비슷하지만 앞으로도 없을 거라는 느낌은 약해요. 주로 '전무후무한 기록'처럼 꾸며 주는 형태로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It implies there was nothing like it before and probably won't be again, so it is used to praise records and achievements strongly. '유례없다' is similar but lacks the 'and never will be' feeling. It is mostly used as a modifier, as in '전무후무한 기록'.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 서비스를 분야별로 전문화하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our company decided to specialize its services by field.
The hospital specialized its departments starting this year.

examples.ko: 작은 가게는 한 가지 메뉴만 전문화해서 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The small shop gained popularity by specializing in just one menu item.

examples.ko: 교육 과정을 전문화하려고 강사를 새로 뽑았어요.
examples.en: They hired new instructors to make the curriculum more specialized.
If you specialize the work, efficiency goes up.
If you don't specialize, it's hard to survive the competition.

explain: '~을 전문화하다'처럼 한 분야를 좁혀 깊이 있게 만든다는 뜻으로 쓰고, 회사나 가게, 학교 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 작은 회사에서 여러 일을 하는 것과 달리 한 가지를 깊이 한다는 느낌이에요. '전문화'라는 명사 형태로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used as '~을 전문화하다' to mean narrowing a field and making it deeper, and it often comes up when talking about companies, shops and schools. It contrasts with doing many jobs at a small company by focusing deeply on one. The noun form '전문화' is also very common.
